intro: Choosing the right area matters more than the hotel itself in Chiang Khan. Here are the main neighborhoods, who each suits, and where to book for your travel style.

blocks.html: Short answer: Chiang Khan is a charming Mekong town of old wooden houses. Most people stay along Chai Khong Road, with its walking street, cafés and dawn sticky-rice alms-giving; for budget and quiet choose the back lanes off Chai Khong; for river rapids and views head to Kaeng Khut Khu at the east end of town.

faq.q: Where in Chiang Khan should I stay?
faq.a: Along Chai Khong Road is best — walk to the walking street, the old wooden houses, cafés and the dawn sticky-rice alms-giving, with the full riverside-town feel. For budget and quiet, stay in the back lanes off Chai Khong, a few minutes’ walk to the river.

faq.q: Do I need to book Chiang Khan ahead in winter?
faq.a: Book well ahead in the cool season (Nov–Jan), especially on long weekends — Chiang Khan gets very busy and riverside rooms sell out fast. Late bookers often find only rooms away from the river or at higher prices.

faq.q: What is there at Kaeng Khut Khu?
faq.a: Kaeng Khut Khu is a rocky rapid in the Mekong at the east end of Chiang Khan, with a local food market (dancing shrimp, coconut candy) and river-view seating. In the dry season the water drops and the rocks show clearly — a nice late-afternoon stop before heading back to Chai Khong Road.
